question: What are the different relationship loading strategies in SQLAlchemy and when do you use each?
title: SQLAlchemy Relationship Loading Strategies
direct_answer: Lazy loading (default): accesses trigger a new query — N+1 problem. Eager loading: selectinload loads related objects in a second IN query (best for async). joinedload loads via JOIN in the same query (best for one-to-one or small to-one). subqueryload uses a subquery (deprecated in favor of selectinload). Dynamic: no longer recommended. Rule: selectinload for collections in async code, joinedload for single related objects.
interviewer_intent: Tests ORM performance awareness — loading strategies are where most ORM-related performance bugs originate.

sections.title: Loading strategies explained
sections.content:
Relationship loading strategy determines when and how SQLAlchemy fetches related objects.

Lazy (default, load='lazy'): related objects load when first accessed. Generates N queries for N parent objects — the N+1 problem. Broken in async code — accessing a lazily-loaded attribute outside an active session raises MissingGreenlet error.

selectinload: fires a second SELECT ... WHERE id IN (...) after the initial query. 2 queries total regardless of result set size. Works perfectly in async. Best default for collections.

joinedload: adds a JOIN to the initial query. Efficient for to-one relationships (user's profile, post's author). Can cause cartesian product for collections.

Controllable per-query: options(selectinload(User.posts)) on a select() statement.

sections.title: Loading strategies
sections.content:
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload, joinedload

# Problem: lazy loading in async triggers MissingGreenlet
async def get_users_broken(db: AsyncSession):
    result = await db.execute(select(User))
    users = result.scalars().all()
    for user in users:
        _ = user.posts  # MissingGreenlet! Can't lazy-load in async

# Fix: selectinload for collections
async def get_users_with_posts(db: AsyncSession) -> list[User]:
    result = await db.execute(
        select(User).options(selectinload(User.posts))  # 2 queries
    )
    return result.scalars().all()

# joinedload for to-one (single related object)
async def get_posts_with_author(db: AsyncSession) -> list[Post]:
    result = await db.execute(
        select(Post).options(joinedload(Post.author))  # 1 query with JOIN
    )
    return result.scalars().unique().all()  # .unique() needed for joins

# Configure default in model
class User(Base):
    posts: Mapped[list['Post']] = relationship(
        back_populates='author',
        lazy='selectin'  # default strategy for this relationship
    )

seo.metaTitle: SQLAlchemy Relationship Loading — selectinload vs joinedload
seo.metaDescription: SQLAlchemy loading strategies: selectinload for async collections, joinedload for to-one relationships, and avoiding N+1 and MissingGreenlet errors.

speakable_v2.hook: The biggest SQLAlchemy performance mistake: relying on lazy loading in async code — it causes MissingGreenlet errors and N+1 query patterns.

beats.content: Lazy loading works in sync code by triggering a new query when you access the attribute. In async SQLAlchemy, that query would need a running event loop context — accessing a lazy relationship outside await raises MissingGreenlet.
selectinload fires a WHERE id IN (...) after the main query. Two queries total, always. Works in async, no cartesian product issues. Best default for collections.
joinedload adds a JOIN to the initial query. One query total. Best for to-one (every post's author). For collections, it creates duplicate rows — use .unique() and prefer selectinload.

speakable_v2.cap: Set lazy='selectin' as the model default for collection relationships in async FastAPI/SQLAlchemy projects. It prevents accidental lazy load bugs without extra per-query options.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with SQLAlchemy's raiseload to catch lazy loading in tests, or deep nested loading patterns.
